summary: Same 60-px clock face with the same three markers and near-identical palette, but the port's pixel-index-to-clock-position mapping is off by one everywhere: every marker sits one pixel clockwise, the hour bar's width breathes 4/5/6 px instead of a constant 5, and the minute and second markers vanish entirely whenever the value is 14, 29, 44 or 59.
observations: Both sides are STATIC under the harness (the wall clock is pinned): motion 0 / motionLit 0 on every captured frame at 20 fps (6 s), 5 fps (60 s), 4 fps (skip 20, 30 s) and 60 fps (5 s); brightnessTrend steady on both; seed 1 and seed 1234 render identically. All judging is therefore per-wall-clock, not per-frame. --wall-clock demonstrably reaches BOTH sides now: every epoch probed changed both renders and both track UTC (no timezone offset on either side).

Structure (default 60-px strip, decoded from --dump). ORIGINAL: dim white background 10,10,10; HOUR = a solid 5-px red bar at indices [h*5 .. h*5+4] using the 12-hour hour (integer, does NOT advance with minutes); MINUTE = a single green pixel at index m; SECOND = a single blue pixel at index s. Draw order is hour, then minute, then second on top (at 03:16:52 the orig shows R15 G16 R17-19 with the green punched into the bar, and at m=52,s=52 the green is hidden under the blue).

PORT structure is the same three markers in the same order with the same widths in principle, but every marker is displaced +1 pixel: at 01:46:40 UTC orig = red[5-9], blue[40], green[46]; port = red[6-10], blue[41], green[47]. Verified at 8 independent wall clocks plus full 60-value second and minute sweeps and a 12-value hour sweep (two sweeps at different m/s to disambiguate overlaps).

The port's displacement is not a clean +1: it is a normalized round-trip that only lands exactly on the four dyadic pixel positions 0, 15, 30, 45 (i/60 exactly representable). Exhaustive second sweep at h=3,m=30: s=0 -> blue at BOTH 0 and 1; s=1..13 -> blue at s+1; s=14 -> NO blue pixel anywhere; s=15 -> blue at 15 and 16; s=16..28 -> s+1; s=29 -> none; s=30 -> 30 and 31; s=44 -> none; s=45 -> 45 and 46; s=59 -> none. Identical law on the minute sweep (m=0/15/30/45 double, m=14/29/44/59 disappear). The original is a clean one-pixel dot at exactly index s (and index m) for all 60 values.

Same law deforms the hour bar. Exhaustive hour sweep (both m=7,s=37 and m=37,s=7 agree). ORIG bar is always exactly 5 px: h=0 [0-4], h=1 [5-9], ... h=11 [55-59]. PORT: h=0 [0-5] 6px, h=1 [6-10] 5px, h=2 [11-14] 4px, h=3 [15-20] 6px, h=4 [21-25] 5px, h=5 [26-29] 4px, h=6 [30-35] 6px, h=7 [36-40] 5px, h=8 [41-44] 4px, h=9 [45-50] 6px, h=10 [51-55] 5px, h=11 [56-59] 4px (clipped at the strip end). The 6/5/4 cycle is exactly the +1 shift plus the four exact positions being double-counted.

Visible consequence on real hardware (where the clock advances): the port's second dot would blink OUT for one full second four times a minute (s=14,29,44,59) and show as a 2-px wide dot at s=0,15,30,45; the minute dot does the same four times an hour; the hour bar visibly changes width as the hour rolls over. The original's markers are rock-steady 1 px / 5 px at all 60 (resp. 12) values.

Palette. All four colours are fixed constants on both sides (no time dependence -- scanned every pixel of 157 runs, exactly 4 distinct RGBs per side). Background: orig 10,10,10 vs port 7,7,7 (port ~30% dimmer). Hour: orig 255,51,51 = hsv(0.00, 0.80, 1.0) vs port 255,51,75 = hsv(0.98, 0.80, 1.0) -- same saturation/value, hue about 2% short of red so the port's bar is a touch pink/magenta. Minute: orig 51,255,0 = hsv(0.30, 1, 1), a yellow-leaning chartreuse, vs port 0,255,0 = hsv(0.333, 1, 1), pure green. Second: orig 0,51,127 = hsv(0.60, 1, 0.5), a slightly cyan-leaning blue, vs port 0,0,127 = hsv(0.667, 1, 0.5), pure blue at half value. The port has evidently rounded the original's 0.3/0.6 hue constants to exact thirds.

Resolution behaviour (off-default rigs, reported with rig named). At --pixels 120 and --pixels 300 both sides scale the whole face proportionally (300 px, 08:43:20: orig hour [200-224], minute [215-219], second [100-104]; port the same features shifted +1), so both are resolution-scaling rather than fixed-60 -- and the port keeps its +1 shift at every size. At --pixels 30 and --pixels 12 both sides degenerate and degenerate DIFFERENTLY (12 px, 00:00:00 UTC: orig floods all 12 pixels blue while the port shows only blue[0] + red[1]; 12 px, 08:43:20: orig one red pixel at 8, port entirely background). Neither side is usable below ~30 px, so this is a shared weakness rather than a port-specific one, but the two failure shapes do not match.
Control surfaces MATCH: both sides expose zero settable controls (probe run reports '(no settable controls)' for orig and port). No control-surface finding.
No compile or runtime errors on either side in any of the 157 runs; wantsSensors false on both.
feedback: ROOT CAUSE, one fix covers most of the gap: the port is converting the pixel index to a clock position through a normalized round trip (index/pixelCount scaled back up by 60 and floored) instead of comparing the integer pixel index directly. In 16.16 fixed point i/60*60 lands just under i for every i except the exactly-representable 0, 15, 30, 45, so the floor yields i-1 almost everywhere. Compare the raw integer index against the integer second/minute/hour-bar range (or add a half-pixel epsilon before flooring) and the +1 shift, the 4/5/6 hour-bar width wobble and the 14/29/44/59 dropouts all disappear together.

Concrete acceptance test after the fix, on the default 60-px strip: for every second s in 0..59 the blue pixel must be at index s and nowhere else (exactly one lit blue pixel, never zero, never two). Same for the green minute pixel over m in 0..59. The red hour bar must be exactly 5 px wide at [h*5 .. h*5+4] for all 12 hours -- currently widths are 6,5,4,6,5,4,6,5,4,6,5,4 for h=0..11.

Palette constants to match exactly (orig RGB on the 60-px rig): background 10,10,10 (port is 7,7,7 -- raise the background value by about 1.4x); hour bar 255,51,51, i.e. hue 0.0 with saturation 0.8 (port renders 255,51,75, hue ~0.98 -- its hour hue is a hair negative/short of pure red); minute 51,255,0, i.e. hue 0.30 not 1/3 (port's pure 0,255,0 is visibly greener than the original's chartreuse); second 0,51,127, i.e. hue 0.60 not 2/3, value 0.5 (port's 0,0,127 is pure blue). Do not 'tidy' 0.3/0.6 into thirds -- the original's slightly-off hues are the intended look.
Keep the original's draw order (hour bar first, minute over it, second on top) -- the port already does this correctly and the punched-out marker inside the hour bar is part of the look.

The hour bar must stay on the INTEGER 12-hour value and must not creep with the minutes: at 03:07 and 03:37 the original's bar is at [15-19] both times. The port also does this correctly today; do not 'improve' it into a smooth hour hand.

Lower priority: below ~30 px both sides fall apart, but differently (at 12 px the original floods the whole strip with the second colour at s=0 while the port goes dark). If the port is ever expected to run on short strips, matching the original's degenerate behaviour there is a separate task; the default 60-px rig is what matters.
experiments: rj104-min-0 .. rj104-min-59 (full 60-value minute sweep at h=3, s=52)
